propositions: Full-suite scheduler load causes intermittent false stall classification of git-fetch dribble tests due to delayed fixture wake-ups reducing actual throughput below the configured rate.
Tests apply an artificial 2-second low-speed window uniformly to both zero-byte stall controls and above-floor negative controls, conflating two distinct test concerns.
Cumulative catch-up pacing fixes repeated late wake-ups but cannot recover after libcurl aborts during a single uninterrupted scheduler gap that exceeds the configured window.

The fix separates fast 2-second stall detection for zero-byte cases from one production 10-second window integration test with real Git/libcurl, and adds a deterministic unit test of cumulative bytes-owed math.
Production git-fetch configuration (10-second window, floor rate) must remain unchanged; only test-layer controls and coverage are refactored.
